quotes.text: The measure of a dashboard is not whether it is viewed, it is whether someone can decide with it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Replaces adoption metrics with a decision-based test for dashboards.

quotes.text: A semantic model is not a power BI feature. It's an organizational contract. It's the place where you stop pretending raw tables have meaning, and you explicitly define it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear explanation of why semantic models matter beyond the tool.

quotes.text: Power BI didn't die, it got demoted. In the dashboard era, power BI was the destination. You trained people to go to the report, you built navigation like it was a website and you treated the canvas as the product.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the shift of Power BI from destination to evidence layer.

quotes.text: Decision velocity is the metric that survives contact with reality. Time from question to action. That's it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the episode's new north-star metric in one line.

quotes.text: If the CEO asks co-pilot instead of your dashboard, your operating model already changed. Not next quarter, not in the future, but already.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pointed warning for data leaders about where the interface has moved.

takeaways: Executives ask for decisions, not numbers, so the real cost of a reporting system is decision latency from question to action.
Power BI and Fabric semantic models become the governed meaning contract and evidence layer behind Copilot and data agent answers.
Trustworthy answers need data contracts, controlled query surfaces such as verified answers, identity boundaries, provenance and observability.
hook: Executives still ping a person instead of opening the dashboard, because they want answers, not canvases. This episode is for BI, data and IT leaders working with Power BI, Fabric and Copilot in Microsoft 365. You will learn why semantic models, verified answers and identity-aware governance matter more than new reports, and how to measure decision velocity instead of adoption.
